Every step is onlyIfVisible so the flow is idempotent.
WHY THE POST-LOGIN WAIT IS SHORT (12s, not 45s).
auth.setup.ts logs in to EVERY registered app on the first browser replay after the state's
TTL lapses, and it writes EMPTY_STATE when a login fails. For this portal the login is
EXPECTED to fail while the account has TOTP enabled, so that timeout is paid on every TTL
window by whichever replay happens to run first — including replays that never touch this
portal. A real login reaches the shell in a couple of seconds, so 12s is generous for the
success path while keeping the guaranteed-failure path cheap.
Consequently .auth/<slug>.json for this portal is expected to hold EMPTY_STATE, and NO spec
should use stateFor('<slug>'). Specs use the hand-captured, role-suffixed state that
auth.setup.ts does not own — .auth/<slug>-<role>.json, written by scripts/capture-state.mjs
and resolved via capturedStateFor(). This mirrors how pages/eptts-web/roles.ts already keeps
non-admin states out of setup's way.
ON 2FA: THE OTP REQUIREMENT WAS REMOVED FROM THE DEVSIM ACCOUNTS ON 2026-09-08.
Until then every live account (janssen2@masar.com, and the admin) answered the password step
with a One-time code prompt, which no declarative step can satisfy -- auth.setup.ts timed out
and wrote EMPTY_STATE every run. It is gone now, verified by this flow completing unattended,
so the normal path works again and specs use stateFor('<slug>').
If it ever comes back, the fallback is already built rather than needing rediscovery:
node automation-hub/scripts/capture-state.mjs --portal <slug> --role admin
writes .auth/<slug>-<role>.json, which auth.setup.ts does not own and cannot overwrite, and
lib/captured-state.ts reads it with an actionable error when it is missing or stale. An admin
capture is also mirrored onto .auth/<slug>.json so existing projects keep working.
